dedupe_keys.name: enatech natural hazard triggered technological accidents database

description: eNATECH is the Joint Research Centre's database of Natech accidents: technological accidents triggered by a natural hazard or disaster that cause fires, explosions or toxic releases of hazardous substances. It collects information on such accidents worldwide so that reports can be searched and analysed for lessons learned, prompted by events such as the 2002 European floods and Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. Each record gives the date, the natural hazard (for example wildfire, tropical cyclone or extreme temperature), the named event, the affected facility or asset type, the release and its consequences; recent entries in 2024 include a typhoon affecting a fuel tanker and a wildfire at a retail store. The database is free to search on the web, and the JRC asks users to cite it as "eNatech (year of access), European Commission Joint Research Centre"; a user guide (Necci and Krausmann, 2022, doi:10.2760/88277) documents it. The JRC does not guarantee accuracy or completeness. Caveats: entries depend on public reports and are not exhaustive. For simulation it is an event record for natech fragility, cascading multi-hazard and emergency response studies of industrial and energy facilities. Related catalogue records include eMARS, ARIA and the JRC RAPID-N tool.
